About me

I’m Aqil, a Computer Engineering student at Temasek Polytechnic with a background in aerospace avionics. At Yokogawa Electric Asia, I supported equipment troubleshooting and functional testing. I enjoy work that lets me trace faults hands-on, whether that means checking how a circuit is wired, testing equipment or reviewing the code that controls it. I’m interested in aerospace technician roles, hardware troubleshooting and aviation operations.

Engineering projects

Embedded systems · Jun–Aug 2026

Occupancy and Ventilation Control System

Ever walked into a packed canteen or indoor event space and felt how quickly it got hot and stuffy?

I designed a PIC16F18877-based prototype to help staff track occupancy and manage ventilation in small indoor spaces. Infrared sensors count people entering and leaving, and a buzzer and red LED alert staff when the space reaches capacity.

The system monitors temperature and humidity alongside the headcount. It adjusts the fan speed and operates a motorised ventilation flap as the space gets busier, warmer or more humid.

  • Embedded C
  • PIC16F18877
  • MPLAB X

Try the occupancy and ventilation demo

Move the sliders to see how the LED, fan, ventilation flap and capacity buzzer respond.

Green LED · Normal conditions | Fan: Low | Flap: Closed | Buzzer: Off Example settings for this simulation. Ventilation increases at 12 people, 31 °C or 75% humidity. The capacity alert activates at 15 people.
How the prototype works

I programmed the PIC16F18877 in Embedded C using MPLAB X. The IR sensors detect people entering and leaving, and the seven-segment display shows the running count. The MCP9701A temperature sensor and DHT11 humidity sensor supply readings for the 16×2 LCD.

The controller uses PWM and an L298N motor driver to adjust the DC fan speed. A separate motor simulates opening the ventilation flap. Green, yellow and red LEDs show the operating state, and the buzzer sounds at capacity.

Software development · Jun–Aug 2026

HDB Utilities Billing and Payment Application

Ever opened your utilities bill and wondered how much of the total came from electricity and how much came from water?

I built a Python application that brings those charges into one view. The app calculates the bill using water and electricity usage and the selected billing period, then lets users review the total before proceeding to payment.

  • Python
  • Spyder
  • Object-oriented programming

Build a sample utility bill

Enter usage or change the billing period to see how the total moves.

S$45.00 electricity + S$12.00 water = S$57.00 Demo uses illustrative rates. Payments are part of the coursework application.
How I built the application

I drew a class diagram to plan the application, then used Python in Spyder to build the interface and backend. I implemented the billing logic for peak, off-peak and festive periods and connected the review and payment steps.

I designed five production jigs in Tinkercad, working from measurements of the real components. For each one I chose a print material and estimated the print time, then helped investigate any unexpected print results.
